title: Correct Booking, Wrong Tour? Verification vs. Validation Explained
afterParagraph: Does the design control what external parties need to know, provide, acknowledge, decide, and record without exposing them to contradictory instructions? Walk through the visible guest experience and ask a partner to demonstrate the handoff in their own words.
rationale: A booking can satisfy recorded requirements while the actual route still fails the traveller’s intended need; this illustrative accessibility example makes the distinction concrete.
evidence: Public video description and article paragraph; not a full transcript audit.

title: Ho Ren So DMC Excursion Communication Short
afterParagraph: A useful guest update usually acknowledges the situation, states what is known without speculation, explains the action under way, gives a realistic next update, and provides a way to obtain help. It should not expose another guest’s information, assign blame before facts are established, or promise an outcome outside the communicator’s authority.
rationale: An illustrative excursion road closure shows reporting confirmed facts, informing affected teams, consulting within decision rights and closing the loop with one approved update.
evidence: Public video description and article paragraph; not a full transcript audit.
